title: Andaman Islands — the complete guide
selection: The Andaman pages covered only the capital, the two main beach islands and a few sights. This pack adds the main beaches of Havelock and Neil, the capital's museums and islands, water sports, the road north (Baratang, Rangat, Mayabunder, Diglipur, Saddle Peak) and Little Andaman, with 3 itineraries and 9 guides — researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism) and Wikipedia.

RAD1.claim: Radhanagar Beach on Swaraj Dweep is a Blue Flag-certified beach known for white sand, turquoise water and forest behind it.

evidence.quote: it has been awarded the Blue Flag beach certification
The beach is known for its white sand, clear turquoise waters, and dense tropical forests.
Seek tranquility on Havelock Island's Radhanagar Beach, a pristine paradise with soft sands and crystal-clear waters.

ELE1.claim: Elephant Beach on Swaraj Dweep is a snorkelling favourite; a trail through the mangroves also leads there.

evidence.quote: One can go snorkelling at Elephant Beach at Havelock Island.
Another trekking trail is from Havelock passing through the mangrove meshes to reach Elephant beach.

KAL1.claim: Kalapathar Beach is known for its dramatic black rocks.

evidence.quote: Visit nearby beaches like Kalapathar, renowned for its dramatic black volcanic rocks

HAV1.claim: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock) and Shaheed Dweep (Neil) are the main islands for scuba diving; you can also kayak Havelock's mangrove creeks.

evidence.quote: Havelock and Neil Islands are prime destinations for scuba diving.
Paddle through the mangrove creeks of Havelock Island on a clear kayak.

BHA1.claim: Bharatpur Beach on Shaheed Dweep has coral reefs and marine life close to shore.

evidence.quote: Go to Neil Island’s Bharatpur Beach and get lost in the colourful coral reefs and rich marine life.

LAX1.claim: Laxmanpur Beach has limestone formations and the natural rock arch locally called the Howrah Bridge.

evidence.quote: the natural rock formation locally known as the Howrah Bridge on the Lakshmanpur Beach is simply stunning
encountering natural wonders like the limestone formations at Laxmanpur Beach

SIT1.claim: Bharatpur and Sitapur beaches suit swimming and sunsets.

evidence.quote: You can stroll on the beautiful beaches at Bharatpur and Sitapur, perfect for activities like swimming, sunbathing, or just soaking in the views of breathtaking sunsets.

CSM1.claim: Chatham Island, where British presence began, now houses the Chatham Saw Mill, one of Asia's oldest.

evidence.quote: British presence was established on Chatham Island - now the city of Port Blair on these islands.
Once a penal settlement, it now houses the Chatham Saw Mill, one of Asia’s oldest.

ANM1.claim: The Anthropological Museum holds tribal artefacts, including the only existing Jarawa skeleton; an open-air section shows traditional dwellings.

evidence.quote: an invaluable repository of tribal artifacts that offer a window into the indigenous ways of life
Sri Vijaya Puram's Anthropological Museum preserves the only existing skeleton of a Jarawa
the open-air Anthropological Settlement Museum exhibits traditional dwellings

SAM1.claim: The navy's Samudrika Marine Museum displays the islands' marine biodiversity.

evidence.quote: the Samudrika Marine Museum displays the biodiversity found on the islands

NBI1.claim: North Bay Island, a short boat ride from Sri Vijaya Puram, is the main water-sports spot — scuba, glass-bottom boats and sea walking — and is pictured on the ₹20 note.

evidence.quote: North Bay Island, Port Blair's premier water sports destination, provides activities including scuba diving and glass-bottom boat rides
The scenic North Bay Island , depicted on the Indian 20 rupee note

SEA1.claim: Sea walking at North Bay Island and Havelock needs no swimming skills.

evidence.quote: Port Blair's North Bay Island introduces visitors to sea walking – a unique adventure that requires no swimming skills.
One of the biggest attractions in Andaman is the underwater walk at North Bay Island and Havelock Island.

VIP1.claim: Viper Island, 4 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram, held the old Viper jail, where Sher Ali Afridi was hanged after assassinating Viceroy Lord Mayo in 1872.

evidence.quote: The island lies 4 km (2 mi) west of Sri Vijaya Puram
was hanged after he assassinated Lord Mayo , the Viceroy of India , on February 8, 1872

JBR1.claim: Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands in the marine park have the best views of Andaman's coral reefs.

evidence.quote: Head to Jolly Buoy Island or Red Skin Island for the best view of the multicoloured coral reefs that Andaman is famous for.

MHT1.claim: An easy 3 km trek runs from Mount Harriet to the Kala Pathar rocks; Mount Harriet is South Andaman's highest peak at 365 m.

evidence.quote: The easy 3-kilometer trek from Mount Harriet to Kala Pathar rocks rewards hikers with stunning views on clear days.
towards Mount Harriet where the highest peak in South Andaman stands tall at an astounding 365m

SCU1.claim: Havelock's coral reefs are reached by a short ferry from the capital; snorkelling, scuba and many other water sports are on offer.

evidence.quote: A short ferry ride whisks you to Havelock Island, where brightly coloured coral reefs teeming with colourful fish await exploration through snorkelling or scuba diving.
Swimming, snorkelling, scuba diving, banana boat rides, parasailing, underwater walking, jet skiing

BAR1.claim: Baratang, 150 km north of the capital, has limestone caves, mangrove creeks and India's only known mud volcanoes.

evidence.quote: The island lies 150 km (93 mi) north of Port Blair.
Beaches, mangrove creeks, limestone caves , and mud volcanoes are some of the physical features.
Baratang contains the only known examples of mud volcanoes in India.

RNG1.claim: Rangat is 210 km from the capital and 70 km south of Mayabunder.

evidence.quote: Rangat is 210 km from Port Blair and 70 km south of Mayabunder.

CUT1.claim: Cuthbert Bay near Rangat is an important turtle-nesting beach, especially December to February.

evidence.quote: Cutbert Bay Beach at Rangat serves as an important turtle breeding site
Cuthbert Bay is an important turtle nesting ground, especially from December to February.

MAY1.claim: Mayabunder, once a settlement for freed political prisoners, has quiet beaches such as Karmatang and Avis Island and mangrove forests.

evidence.quote: Mayabunder served as a settlement for freed political prisoners
Beaches like Karmatang Beach and Avis Island Beach mesmerize visitors
The mangrove forests surrounding Mayabunder harbour a rich diversity of flora and fauna

AVI1.claim: Avis Island is uninhabited and open only with special permission from the forest department.

evidence.quote: Avis is uninhabited and open only with special permission from the forest department.

DIG1.claim: Diglipur, 298 km north of the capital, sits on the Kalpong, the islands' only river; Saddle Peak and the Alfred Caves are nearby.

evidence.quote: 298 kilometres (185 miles) north of Port Blair
It is crossed by the Kalpong River , the only river of the Andaman islands.
it is open to those going to the limestone Alfred Caves in Diglipur

DIG2.claim: Ram Nagar beach near Diglipur is known for sea-turtle nesting from December to February.

evidence.quote: is famous for sea turtle nesting from December to February

SAD1.claim: Saddle Peak, near Diglipur, is the archipelago's highest point; its national park was set up in 1979 and covers 32.54 sq km.

evidence.quote: you must also visit the Saddle Peak, the highest point of the archipelago.
It was set up in 1979
It covers an area of 32.54 square kilometres

LAN1.claim: Little Andaman, 88 km south of the capital, is the group's fourth-largest island (about 734 sq km), with rainforest, beaches and waterfalls.

evidence.quote: It lies 88 km (55 mi) south of Port Blair
is the fourth largest island in the group of islands at Andaman and Nicobar, with an area of about 734 square kilometers
Little Andaman Island has white sandy beaches and bewitching waterfalls.

LAN2.claim: Little Andaman offers surfing, creek boating and visits to an elephant logging plantation.

evidence.quote: Little Andaman offers surfing, boating through the creeks, and visits to an elephant logging plantation.

BUT1.claim: Butler Bay, 14 km from the Hut Bay jetty, is popular for coral viewing and surfing.

evidence.quote: Butler Bay, 14 km from the Hut Bay Jetty, is a beach popular among tourists due to coral viewing, surfing and other marine activities.

ST_FEST.claim: The administration holds a 10-day Island Tourism Festival every year, with cultural performances.

evidence.quote: Every year, Andaman and Nicobar administration hosts the Island Tourism Festival; an exciting 10-day festival

ST_CRAFT.claim: Local crafts include coconut-shell lamps and jewellery, seashell art, woodcraft and palm mats.

evidence.quote: using coconut shells as raw material to craft stunning decorative items such as table lamps, finger bowls and unique jewellery items
woodcraft and palm mats which showcase local artisans

ST_FOOD.claim: Try grilled lobster, coconut fish curry with rice, and tandoori fish.

evidence.quote: Lobsters grilled to perfection, basted with butter and local herbs
The staple diet of many locals includes rice and fish curry.
cooked in a rich coconut milk base with a mix of tangy tamarind and aromatic spices

ST_FERRY.claim: Most mainland flights land too late for the same-day fast ferries to Havelock and Neil, so plan a night in the capital.

evidence.quote: practically all flights from the Indian mainland arrive too late to connect to the hi-speed Makruzz ferries

ST_ATR.claim: The Andaman Trunk Road passes a restricted zone; tourists may use it for trips north, such as to the Alfred Caves.

evidence.quote: While the Andaman Trunk Road remains a restricted zone for tourists, it is open to those going to the limestone Alfred Caves in Diglipur.

A_AN2.claim: Most foreign visitors no longer need a Restricted Area Permit for the 29 islands removed from the RAP regime; 11 more are RAP-free for day visits until 31 December 2027. Citizens of Afghanistan, China and Pakistan, and people of those origins, still need a RAP approved in advance.

evidence.quote: The foreign nationals are not required to obtain a Restricted Area Permit (RAP) for visiting the 29 islands in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands that have been excluded from the RAP regime.
Additionally, 11 islands have been exempted from the RAP requirement for day visits only, and this exemption is valid up to 31/12/2027.
However, this relaxation is not applicable to nationals belonging to the Prior Reference Category (PRC) countries, namely Afghanistan, China (including Hong Kong and Macau), and Pakistan.

A_AN3.claim: Reserved forests, wildlife sanctuaries and tribal reserves need separate approvals, and RAP applications are made online through the FRRO portal.

evidence.quote: Separate approvals from the competent authority shall continue to be required for visiting Reserved Forests, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Tribal Reserves.
Applications for RAP may be submitted online at https://indianfrro.gov.in

A_AN4.claim: The Jarawa, a protected tribe of South and Middle Andaman, shun outside contact; any attempt to interact with them is illegal.

evidence.quote: Any attempt to interact with the isolated tribe, who themselves shun contact with outsiders, is deemed illegal.

A_AN5.claim: Temperatures stay around 23–31 °C all year; rain comes with the monsoons, and tropical cyclones are common in late summer.

evidence.quote: the average ranging from 23 to 31 °C (73 to 88 °F)
The rainfall is dependent on the monsoons and tropical cyclones are common in late summer.

A_AN6.claim: Incredible India makes the case for the monsoon (late May to end July): greener landscapes, fewer visitors and hotel discounts.

evidence.quote: Come monsoons (between late May to end July)
the lush green vegetation and scenic beauty come alive, the tourist rush is over and hoteliers offer attractive discounts

A_AN8.claim: Commercial fishing is banned in Andaman waters to protect dugongs, giant sea turtles and corals.

evidence.quote: commercial fishing in the waters surrounding the Andaman Islands is banned

A_SV1.claim: Sri Vijaya Puram — Port Blair until it was renamed on 13 September 2024 — is the capital, about 1,190 km from Chennai and 1,255 km from Kolkata.

evidence.quote: On 13 September 2024, the Government of India officially renamed the city to Sri Vijaya Puram.
It is located approximately 1,190 km (740 mi) from Chennai and 1,255 km (780 mi) from Kolkata in mainland India .

A_SV2.claim: Veer Savarkar International Airport is the islands' main airport.

evidence.quote: The town is home to the Veer Savarkar International Airport

A_SV4.topic: Chatham Saw Mill and Corbyn's Cove
A_SV4.claim: Chatham Island has one of Asia's oldest sawmills; Corbyn's Cove is a palm-fringed beach a few km south of town.

evidence.quote: it now houses the Chatham Saw Mill, one of Asia’s oldest
Sparkling white sand and gentle waves awaits you at Corbyn's Cove Beach

A_SV6.claim: Try grilled lobster, coconut fish curry, barbecued prawns and squid fry.

evidence.quote: Lobsters grilled to perfection, basted with butter and local herbs
The curry is made with fresh catch, typically cooked in a rich coconut milk base with a mix of tangy tamarind and aromatic spices.

A_SV9.claim: Local crafts include coconut-shell lamps and jewellery, cane baskets and shell work.

evidence.quote: local artisans using coconut shells as raw material to craft stunning decorative items such as table lamps, finger bowls and unique jewellery items

A_SW1.claim: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock) is best known for Radhanagar Beach, or Beach No. 7, a Blue Flag-certified beach.

evidence.quote: Swaraj Dweep (previously Havelock Island), known for its powdery white sand beaches and turquoise waters
Radhanagar Beach on the western coast, also known as Number 7 Beach
it has been awarded the Blue Flag beach certification

A_SW3.claim: Government ferries and private catamarans link Swaraj Dweep with Sri Vijaya Puram and Shaheed Dweep.

evidence.quote: The island's transportation infrastructure is anchored by regular government and high-speed private catamaran ferries

A_NE1.claim: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is quieter, with Bharatpur, Sitapur and Laxmanpur beaches and a natural rock arch.

evidence.quote: Shaheed Dweep (formerly Neil Island)
You can stroll on the beautiful beaches at Bharatpur and Sitapur
the natural rock formation locally known as the Howrah Bridge on the Lakshmanpur Beach is simply stunning

A_NE2.claim: The island is easily explored by bicycle.

evidence.quote: Explore the island by bicycle, traversing scenic pathways

A_NE4.claim: Fresh seafood blends Indian and South-East Asian flavours, and forest trails cross the interior.

evidence.quote: The dishes here are a fusion of Indian and Southeast Asian flavours
the island offers plenty of opportunities for hiking and trekking

A_CJ1.claim: The Cellular Jail was built between 1896 and 1906 to hold political prisoners in solitary confinement — 'Kala Pani'.

evidence.quote: Although the prison complex itself was constructed between 1896 and 1906
Known as Kala Pani, or "Black Waters,"

A_CJ4.claim: Incredible India lists the light and sound show in Hindi at 5:50 pm daily and in English at 6:50 pm on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

evidence.quote: Cellular Jail Light & Sound (Hindi) - 5:50 PM (All days)
Cellular Jail Light & Sound (English) - 6:50 PM (Mon, Wed, Fri)

A_RO1.claim: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island) was the British administrative headquarters until an earthquake in 1941; it was renamed in December 2018.

evidence.quote: NSCB Island once thrived as an administrative hub of the British colonial government before suffering a catastrophic earthquake in 1941.
In December 2018, this island was renamed as Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island

A_MG2.claim: Incredible India lists 9 am–3 pm, closed Mondays.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:00 AM
Closing time - 03:00 PM
Mondays closed

A_MG3.claim: The park is a strictly enforced no-plastic zone.

evidence.quote: all within a strictly enforced no-plastic zone

A_MG4.claim: Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands, open to visitors alternately for six months each, are the places to see the reefs.

evidence.quote: Head to Jolly Buoy Island or Red Skin Island for the best view of the multicoloured coral reefs
The islands are open for tourists alternately for six months each.

tips: Start very early from the capital to reach Baratang's convoy times.

itineraries.title: Andaman in 7 days: the complete trip
itineraries.summary: The capital's history, Netaji Island and North Bay, three days on Havelock and Neil, and the marine park's reefs.
itineraries.seoDescription: A week in the Andamans: the Cellular Jail and light show, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island, North Bay, Havelock, Neil, Mount Harriet and Jolly Buoy's reefs.

plan.overview: Capital, islands and reefs in one week.
plan.transport: Taxis in the capital; ferries between islands; boats from Wandoor.
plan.season: October to May for calm seas.

guides.title: How to reach the Andaman Islands
guides.summary: Flights, distances and the first-night rule for ferries.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Andaman: Flights & Ferries
guides.seoDescription: How to reach the Andamans: flights to Sri Vijaya Puram, distances from Chennai and Kolkata, and why to plan a first night in the capital.

body.intro: Almost everyone arrives by air at Sri Vijaya Puram, then takes ferries onward.

sections.heading: By air
sections.text: Veer Savarkar International Airport in Sri Vijaya Puram is the main gateway. The capital is about 1,190 km from Chennai and 1,255 km from Kolkata.

sections.heading: Onward to the islands
sections.text: Government ferries and private catamarans link the capital with Swaraj and Shaheed Dweep. Most mainland flights land too late for the fast ferries, so plan your first night in Sri Vijaya Puram.

guides.title: Getting around the Andaman Islands
guides.summary: Ferries, bicycles and the long road north.
guides.seoTitle: Getting Around the Andamans: Ferries & Roads
guides.seoDescription: Getting around the Andamans: inter-island ferries, cycling on Neil, and the Andaman Trunk Road to Baratang, Rangat and Diglipur.

body.intro: Islands are linked by sea; the north is reached by a long road through the forest.

sections.heading: Between islands
sections.text: Government ferries and private catamarans run between the capital, Havelock and Neil.

sections.heading: On the islands
sections.text: Neil is small enough to explore by bicycle.

sections.heading: Going north
sections.text: The Andaman Trunk Road is restricted but open to tourists heading north. Rangat is 210 km from the capital; Diglipur is 298 km.

guides.title: Best time to visit the Andaman Islands
guides.summary: Weather, monsoon deals, turtle season and the festival.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Andaman: Season by Season
guides.seoDescription: When to visit the Andamans: 23–31 °C all year, monsoon discounts, turtle nesting December–February and the Island Tourism Festival.

body.intro: The islands are warm all year; the choice is between calm seas, monsoon quiet or turtle season.

sections.heading: Weather
sections.text: Temperatures stay around 23–31 °C all year; rain comes with the monsoons, and tropical cyclones are common in late summer.

sections.heading: Monsoon
sections.text: Incredible India makes the case for late May to end July: greener islands, fewer visitors and hotel discounts.

sections.heading: Turtle season
sections.text: December to February is turtle-nesting season at Cuthbert Bay and near Diglipur.

sections.heading: Festival
sections.text: The administration holds a 10-day Island Tourism Festival every year.

guides.title: Andaman permits and rules
guides.summary: RAP, protected areas and the Jarawa reserve.
guides.seoTitle: Andaman Permits: RAP, Protected Areas & Rules
guides.seoDescription: Andaman permits: which islands need a Restricted Area Permit, approvals for forests and tribal reserves, the Jarawa rules and Avis Island.

body.intro: Most visitors no longer need a permit for the main islands, but protected areas have their own rules.

sections.heading: Restricted Area Permit
sections.text: Most foreign visitors no longer need a RAP for the 29 islands removed from it; protected forests, sanctuaries and tribal reserves need separate approval, applied for online.

sections.heading: Jarawa reserve
sections.text: The Jarawa shun outside contact; any attempt to interact with them is illegal.

sections.heading: Special permission
sections.text: Avis Island near Mayabunder is open only with forest-department permission.

guides.title: Andaman water sports guide
guides.summary: Where to dive, snorkel, sea walk and see coral.
guides.seoTitle: Andaman Water Sports: Diving, Snorkelling & Sea Walk
guides.seoDescription: Andaman water sports: scuba at Havelock and Neil, snorkelling at Elephant Beach, sea walks at North Bay and coral at Jolly Buoy and Red Skin.

body.intro: The Andamans' reefs are the reason many people come — here is where to see them.

sections.heading: Scuba diving
sections.text: Havelock and Neil are the main dive islands.

sections.heading: Snorkelling
sections.text: Elephant Beach on Havelock is the favourite; Jolly Buoy and Red Skin have the best coral views.

sections.heading: Sea walking
sections.text: At North Bay and Havelock — no swimming needed.

sections.heading: Other sports
sections.text: Glass-bottom boats, parasailing and jet skis are also on offer.

guides.title: The best beaches in the Andamans
guides.seoTitle: Best Andaman Beaches: Havelock, Neil & Beyond
guides.seoDescription: The best Andaman beaches: Radhanagar, Elephant and Kalapathar on Havelock; Bharatpur, Laxmanpur and Sitapur on Neil; Corbyn's Cove and Butler Bay.

body.intro: Every island has its beach character — sunsets, snorkelling or surf.

items.title: Radhanagar
items.body: Blue Flag beach with white sand and forest behind.

items.title: Elephant Beach
items.body: The snorkelling beach.

items.title: Kalapathar
items.body: Black rocks and a quiet shore.

items.title: Bharatpur
items.body: Coral close to shore.

items.title: Laxmanpur
items.body: Limestone and the natural rock arch.

items.title: Sitapur
items.body: Swimming and sunsets.

items.title: Corbyn's Cove
items.body: Palm-fringed beach near the capital.

items.title: Butler Bay
items.body: Surf and coral on Little Andaman.

guides.title: Andaman food and shopping guide
guides.summary: Seafood to try and crafts to bring home.
guides.seoTitle: Andaman Food & Shopping: Seafood and Crafts
guides.seoDescription: What to eat in the Andamans — grilled lobster, coconut fish curry, tandoori fish — and the shell, coconut and cane crafts to buy.

body.intro: Fresh seafood is the highlight, and island crafts make good souvenirs.

sections.heading: Eat
sections.text: Grilled lobster, coconut fish curry with rice, barbecued prawns and squid fry.

sections.heading: On Neil
sections.text: Fresh seafood blends Indian and South-East Asian flavours.

sections.heading: Shop
sections.text: Coconut-shell lamps and jewellery, cane baskets, shell art, woodcraft and palm mats.

guides.title: Havelock or Neil: which island to choose
guides.summary: How Swaraj Dweep and Shaheed Dweep differ.
guides.seoTitle: Havelock vs Neil: Which Andaman Island?
guides.seoDescription: Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) vs Neil (Shaheed Dweep): Radhanagar and diving versus a quieter island you can cycle, with a natural rock arch.

body.intro: Most trips include both, but if you must pick one, this is how they differ.

sections.heading: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock)
sections.text: Bigger and busier: Radhanagar Beach, diving and Elephant Beach snorkelling.

sections.heading: Shaheed Dweep (Neil)
sections.text: Quieter and small enough to cycle, with Bharatpur, Sitapur and Laxmanpur beaches and the natural rock arch.

guides.title: First-time visitor's guide to the Andamans
guides.summary: What to see first, and the rules to know.
guides.seoTitle: First Time in Andaman: What to Know
guides.seoDescription: A first-timer's guide to the Andamans: the Cellular Jail, Netaji Island, Havelock's Radhanagar, permits and the Jarawa rules.

body.intro: A short checklist for a first trip to the islands.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: The Cellular Jail (1896–1906) and its evening light show; the ruins of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island.

sections.heading: Beaches
sections.text: Radhanagar on Havelock is the classic first beach.

sections.heading: Rules
sections.text: Most main islands need no permit; never try to contact the Jarawa; commercial fishing is banned to protect dugongs and turtles.
